model.name: Meta-guard - no requirement is satisfied while any AC lacks a check that can PROVABLY FAIL (fail-closed)
model.description: FIVE instances in one day each shipped as SATISFIED while its property was VIOLATED = a PROCESS DEFECT, not a series of misses: R40.50 (satisfied by a copy behind a value-gate), R40.48 (ACs present but UNENFORCED - 4 contaminations), check-sprint-slug-dir (guard validated the STRAY path), R32.3 (asserted no-re-fork, only checked rendering), R37.12 (asserted no-view-stale, nothing failable). Root: an AC that NAMES a behaviour but has no check that can PROVABLY FAIL is a wish (reminder-not-mechanism); a universally-quantified AC (all X / every X / no X) passes VACUOUSLY forever. The META-GUARD: a requirement may NOT be marked satisfied while any of its ACs lacks a check that can provably go RED - satisfaction is fail-closed. Architect owns the mechanism.
model.designRequired: architect owns the MECHANISM (how each AC references its gate, how the registered stub-must-fail is proven, how fail-closed satisfaction is computed, the wish-sweep). This unit captures the INVARIANT + the PO candidate shape; architect designs + I refine ACs on the design.
model.family: reminder-not-mechanism / false-satisfaction - the SYSTEMIC cure. Generalizes R4 evidence-must-fail (a Test counts only if AST-attached to a failable assertion) + R6 certification-scope from Test-level to AC-level.
model.crossRefNote: The 5 known instances this meta-guard would have caught. Seeds the wish-sweep. Generalizes the R3/R4/R6 gating-canon (session/base-skills/gating-canon.md) to every AC of every requirement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every AC references its GATE (the test/check unit that verifies it). An AC with no gate reference is INCOMPLETE.
That gate must carry a REGISTERED stub-must-fail proving it can go RED (evidence-must-fail at the AC level, generalizing R4). A gate never observed to fail is unproven.

Satisfaction is REFUSED (fail-closed) for any AC whose gate cannot provably fail - an AC with no failable gate is UNSATISFIED, never satisfied-by-default. A requirement is satisfied only when ALL its ACs have a proven-failable gate that is currently GREEN.

A universally-quantified AC (all X / every X / no X) is INADMISSIBLE as-is - it has no finite thing to check and passes vacuously. It MUST be replaced with the ENUMERATED list of X PLUS a divergence cross-check that fails when members diverge (the R37.12 (C) fix generalized: all-current-views -> pin/drawer/tree/scoreboard + any-two-disagree => RED).
A sweep reports EXISTING ACs across the graph that cannot provably fail (the backlog of wishes) so they can be retired or upgraded. The 5 known instances seed it; the sweep count must drain toward 0.

The meta-guard itself is proven failable: seed a requirement with an AC that has NO failable gate and mark it satisfied => the meta-guard goes RED. If the meta-guard cannot bite on a seeded wish, the meta-guard is itself a wish.

(a) NEW or CHANGED ACs are FAIL-CLOSED IMMEDIATELY - no exceptions, no grandfathering. From R40.54 forward, an AC created or edited WITHOUT a failable gate CANNOT be satisfied. stub-must-fail: a newly-added/edited AC with no failable gate that is marked satisfied => RED.

(b) EXISTING ACs the sweep finds unfailable get a DISTINCT VISIBLE state satisfaction-UNVERIFIED - NOT green, NOT falsely unsatisfied, NEVER silently grandfathered. Honest: the work may well be done, we just cannot PROVE it (both-directions: do not inflate, do not erase). stub-must-fail: an existing unfailable AC rendered as GREEN (inflation) OR as UNSATISFIED (erasure) instead of UNVERIFIED => RED.

(c) the sweep drains BY RISK, not alphabetically: user-facing behaviour + invariant-critical properties FIRST (where a wish costs Tron something - exactly like R37.12 cost him a duplicated drawer), housekeeping LAST. stub-must-fail: a drain that resolves a housekeeping UNVERIFIED while a user-facing/invariant-critical UNVERIFIED remains outstanding => RED (risk-order violated).

(d) the satisfaction-UNVERIFIED count is PUBLISHED (auditable + must monotonically shrink); drained is NEVER reported while any remain. stub-must-fail: a drained / 0-remaining claim while the published count > 0 => RED (the false-drained claim, a fresh false-satisfaction of the sweep itself).

model.sweepPolicy: PO ruling (a)-(d) encoded AS ACs so the policy cannot drift into a reminder: (a) new/changed=fail-closed-now; (b) existing=satisfaction-UNVERIFIED distinct state; (c) drain by RISK; (d) publish count, never-false-drained. satisfaction-UNVERIFIED = honest third state (not green, not erased). I own that the state is honest; architect owns the mechanism.
